{{Short description|American cryptographer (1900–1962)}}
{{other uses|Julia Ward (disambiguation)}}

'''Julia Ward''' (December 1900 – June 18, 1962) was the founder of the central reference division{{what|date=April 2025}} of the [[National Security Agency|National Security Agency (NSA)]]. She was inducted into the [[NSA Hall of Honor|Cryptologic Hall of Honor]] in 2002.<ref name="NSA 2002">{{Cite web|url=https://www.nsa.gov/about/cryptologic-heritage/historical-figures-publications/hall-of-honor/2002/jward.shtml|title=Dr. Julia Ward (1900 - 1962) 2002 Inductee|website=www.nsa.gov |access-date=2018-08-14}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2002/06/14/nsa-belatedly-recognizes-six-silent-sentinels/ |title=NSA belatedly recognizes six 'silent sentinels'|work=[[The Baltimore Sun]] |date=July 14, 2002 |first=Ariel |last=Sabar |access-date=2019-01-13 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cryptologicfoundation.org/file_download/inline/1f38f96a-5734-44d8-a1ce-922c1601488c|title=The Link|last=|first=|date=|website=Cryptologic Foundation|access-date=}}</ref>

== Education ==
Ward received her A.B. from [[Bryn Mawr College]] in 1923 and her Ph.D from Bryn Mawr College in 1940.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.brynmawr.edu/cs/history|title=History |website=Bryn Mawr College |access-date=2018-08-14}}</ref> 

== World War II ==
Ward joined the cryptologic service during [[World War II]] and worked for the [[Signal Security Agency]] (the Army's cryptologic organization). She also worked as a librarian and eventually built a collection of [[classified information|classified]] and [[unclassified]] materials for use by analysts. In 1945, she became the deputy chief of the reference section. Within a few years, she turned the section from one that was known as poorly organized, into a section that was widely recognized and highly respected.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=vFYRDgAAQBAJ&pg=PT430 |title=Code Girls: The Untold Story of the American Women Code Breakers of World War II |last=Mundy|first=Liza|date=2017-10-10|publisher=Hachette Books|isbn=9780316352550}}</ref> 

In 1949, Ward was named head of the Collateral Branch, thereby becoming the only female branch head in the [[Office of Operations]]. In 1955, Ward was promoted to deputy chief of NSA's Liaison and Foreign Operations Section.<ref name="NSA 2002" />

== Cryptologic Hall of Honor ==
Ward was inducted into the NSA's Cryptologic Hall of Honor in June 2002 at the National Cryptologic Museum in Baltimore, MD. Bryn Mawr College has a plaque to commemorate her placement in the Hall of Honor.<ref name="NSA 2002" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cia.gov/library/readingroom/search/site/warded?page=3|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180814103102/https://www.cia.gov/library/readingroom/search/site/warded?page=3|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 14, 2018|title=FOIA |website=CIA |access-date=2018-08-14}}</ref>
